checks: Conditional on one coordinate x, the remaining uniform section is an affine copy of the lower-dimensional simplex scaled by 1-x. This includes the deterministic remaining coordinate for N=2. The original marginal is continuous, so the unused endpoint x=1 is harmless.

The condition probability is nondecreasing in x because c/(1-x) is nondecreasing for c in [0,1]. Its covariance with the decreasing event X_i<=c is nonpositive by the independent-copy identity. Iteration takes smaller index sets under the same original law and never assumes coordinate independence.

The affine barycentric description gives lambda_i(-x)=2/(d+1)-lambda_i(x), so x lies in -T exactly when all original lambda_i(x) are at most 2/(d+1). The single-coordinate tail is the volume ratio (1-c)^(N-1) of a scaled simplex, with the endpoints c=0,1 valid.

The derivative of (x-1)log(1-2/x) is -log y+(y-1/y)/2 with y=x/(x-2). This expression is positive for y>1 by its derivative in y. For N>=9 the bound is therefore at most (7/8)^9, and exact integers give 3*7^9<8^9.

With actual A=K=-T and B=T intersect -T, the erosion cutoff is 2/(d+1) for every coordinate and the enclosure is exactly B. Exact finite inclusion-exclusion gives 1, 2/3, 1/2, 46/125, 22/81, 3364/16807 and 151/1024; d=5,6,7 and N>=9 exhaust d>=5.

dependencies.hypotheses: Set A=K=-T and B=T intersect -T in the frozen theorem. These are full-dimensional, B lies in T and -T, and midpoint compatibility follows. The two actual opposite supports are 1, hence every c_i=2/(d+1); the resulting enclosure is B. The finite exact formula is therefore an admissible specialization. Admission depends on the independent approval of the frozen erosion proof.

overlap.comparison: The accepted planar intersection area gives rho_2=2/3 by m=1 in its canonical formula. It has neither the N-coordinate probability bound nor the strict bound for d>=5.

readability: The finite values include d=7 (N=8), the last case before the uniform estimate applies.
review_method: Independent cold proof read of the frozen statement and proof, followed by source and exact dependency comparison and exact rational checks where applicable.
summary: The conditional monotonicity proof gives the stated all-threshold simplex probability inequality. The exact erosion formula and the marginal-tail estimate yield the listed finite constants and the strict bound in every dimension at least five.
